I5.quote: Among the wide variety of existing carbons materials, activated carbons (ACs) exhibit, on average, the highest hydrogen adsorption capacities (up to 7 wt. % at 4 MPa and 77 K) [1,2].

notes: Document is a conference poster (Carbon 2019, Lexington) deposited in HAL; p. 1 is the HAL cover sheet (English and French boilerplate), p. 2 is the poster, entirely English apart from two diagram labels ("Dubinin-Astakhov modifiee", decimal comma "0,1"). not_primary considered and not applied: the poster is not a review, perspective, thesis or patent and it carries experimental data (Figures 1-8), so it is not an abstract without data. I1: the H2 method is given only as the acronym HPVA (high-pressure volumetric analyzer) in the Methodology box; the word volumetric is not printed, so I1 rests on the instrument acronym plus the authors presenting their own measured excess isotherms at 77-273 K, 0.1-14 MPa (Fig. 3 shows markers; Fig. 4 shows data points with MDA fits at 77-273 K). The poster names no uptake basis other than "excess". I3: Fig. 3 gives 77 K and absolute pressure 0-12.4 MPa on the axis; no numeric uptake values appear in the text. I4: surface area is reported only graphically as S_NLDFT (NLDFT surface area from N2 77 K and CO2 273 K isotherms), not as printed numbers; read by eye from the Figure 1 right axis, about 2200 (MSC-30), 2000 (MSP-20), 1610 (SA_1500), 1290 (SA_20), 1250 (TH90I) m2/g. The Methodology box lists a BET surface but gives no BET value. Surface area is for the same five carbons whose H2 isotherms are shown. If a stricter reading requires a printed number, I4 would fail (no_surface_area); I judged a plotted value on a labelled m2/g axis to be reported. retracted: record.json is_retracted false; no retraction notice in the text. duplicate_data: the poster makes no statement that its H2 values were published before (reference [1] is cited only for the 7 wt% introductory figure).
